subject: Week 39: answer every gesture — waving and giving are pre-word turns
bodyText:
This week
Days 271 through 277 close the third quarter. Gesture is where the growth shows: waving bye, shaking his head, arms up to be lifted, handing over an object when you ask — the CDC scores waving and giving on the 12-month checklist, so early appearance is a bonus rather than the bar. Cruising is fluid for many, first independent steps arrive for a few, and first specific words are emerging for some, with the CDC 2022 checkpoint for words beyond mama and dada at 15 months.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Bumps and knocks from cruising falls onto carpet — supervised falls onto forgiving surfaces are how the balance system calibrates.
- [low concern] Waking early to stand up in the crib — drop the mattress to its lowest setting if you have not already, and keep the response short and boring.
- [monitor] No joint attention — he does not follow your point or bring you things to look at — alongside flat, unvaried babble. Two channels quiet at once is the pattern worth documenting.
- [call within 24h] A stomach bug with fewer than five wet diapers in 24 hours, or vomiting that persists past 12 hours.
- [call now] Severe respiratory distress — retractions, grunting, nasal flaring — or fever ≥102F rectal with lethargy; blue lips or unresponsiveness is 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Wave at every arrival and departure and say the word with it — hello on the way in, bye-bye on the way out, the same script from both parents. Waving is a CDC 1-year item and it is acquired by imitation, not instruction. CDC 1-year milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
- Put words on the gestures he already owns: arms up becomes up, a head shake becomes all done, an offered toy becomes thank you. Mapping language onto a signal he already controls is easier than asking him to learn both at once, and it keeps the exchange bidirectional — turns, not volume, are what the language data support. Romeo et al. 2018 (PubMed): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Introduce a single-shape knob puzzle — one large piece, one hole. Removing and replacing the piece is a spatial and fine-motor task right at the edge of what he can do, and the knob is what makes it reachable with a thumb-and-finger grip.
- Bank one outdoor block a day through the wet stretch — a carrier walk or a blanket on the playground grass. It costs nothing, delivers vestibular and visual input a living room cannot, and hands you a 30-minute narration slot.

Upcoming
- Day 252-280 (Jan 18–Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit — nine days left in the window. If the visit is behind you, chase the loose ends this week: hemoglobin result, influenza #2 if this is his first season, and anything the ASQ-3 screen flagged.
- Day 280 (Mon Feb 15, 2027): the window closes and the next scheduled well visit is at 12 months — anything arising between now and May routes through a sick visit or the triage line.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Plays peekaboo (initiates by covering and uncovering face)
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Active game initiation, not just smiling when you hide. Demonstrates object permanence in action.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/plays-peekaboo/complete

- Plays games like pat-a-cake
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Imitative gesture game. Joint attention + motor imitation.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/plays-pat-a-cake/complete

- Waves bye-bye
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Intentional gesture with social meaning.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/waves-bye/complete

- Calls a parent 'mama' or 'dada' or another name
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Specifically referring to a person, not generalized babble. First true word for many babies.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/calls-parent-by-name/complete

- Understands 'no' (pauses or stops when you say it)
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Receptive language. Compliance is a much later milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/understands-no/complete
